practiceProblems.description: Read $T$ integers and print each integer on its own line. This warm-up reinforces the complete judge flow: parse input, process each case, and produce exactly the required output.

practiceProblems.title: Arithmetic progression middle term
practiceProblems.description: Given $A$ and $C$ with $A\le C$, determine whether an integer $B$ exists such that $A,B,C$ form an arithmetic progression. Output $B$ when it exists; otherwise output $-1$.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given $A$ and $C$ with $A\le C$, determine whether an integer $B$ exists such that $A,B,C$ form an arithmetic progression. Output $B$ when it exists; otherwise output $-1$.
practiceProblems.inputFormat: The first line contains $T$. Each test case contains two integers $A$ and $C$.
practiceProblems.outputFormat: For each test case, print the required middle term $B$, or $-1$ if $C-A$ is odd.

practiceProblems.title: Problem (Shoes)
practiceProblems.description: Chef needs one left shoe and one right shoe for each of $N$ friends. He already has $M$ left shoes. Find the minimum number of additional shoes needed to make $N$ complete pairs.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Chef needs one left shoe and one right shoe for each of $N$ friends. He already has $M$ left shoes. Find the minimum number of additional shoes needed to make $N$ complete pairs.
practiceProblems.inputFormat: The first line contains $T$. Each test case contains two integers $N$ and $M$.
practiceProblems.outputFormat: For each test case, print the minimum number of shoes Chef must buy.

sampleTestCases.explanation: He needs $N$ right shoes and enough left shoes to reach $N$: $N+\max(0,N-M)$.
